Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the South African players. Devon Conway and Tom Latham are the two openers for New Zealand. Dane Paterson has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
.. THIRD INNINGS ...

On the other hand, it is a very sorry-looking batting scorecard for South Africa. They were just not able to handle this strong Kiwi attack. However, some of the batters like Edward Moore, Zubayr Hamza, and David Bedingham got starts but could not convert them. The Proteas were not able to stitch up any significant partnerships in the middle and Keegan Petersen was the top scorer with 45, and he too missed out on a half-century by playing a loose shot like many of the other batters. They have been bundled out for 162 and still trail by 349 runs. Now, they will hope that their bowlers can put on a better show and at least restrict the Kiwis from setting up a mammoth target. Join us in a bit for New Zealand's second innings.

Tom Latham is running back, which means that New Zealand will not be enforcing the follow-on. We expected a strong bowling effort from the Kiwis, and they did not disappoint. The pacers set the tone with four wickets upfront right before Stumps on Day 2 with Kyle Jamieson picking up a couple. It was Matt Henry who got the crucial breakthroughs in the morning session with two in one over and ended up with three in total. However, after that, it was all about the spinners. Mitchell Santner and Rachin Ravindra got a lot of turn on this pitch and shared five wickets between them to wrap things up here.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! That's it! South Africa are all out at a paltry 162. Nicely floated delivery on the stumps on a fuller length, Dane Paterson plays all over it on the wrong line and the ball sneaks past his outside edge before breaking into the stumps. A convincing bowling performance by the Blackcaps as they still have a lead of 349 runs with them. Rachin Ravindra finishes with a couple of scalps as well. Overall, a fantastic outing for him and the Kiwis. A sorry-looking score for South Africa.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the post-Lunch session to begin. The Umpires make their way out to the middle and the New Zealand fielders too, spread out to the field. Keegan Petersen and Duanne Olivier to resume their innings for the Proteas. Kyle Jamieson to bowl the first over of the second session. Let's play...
...DAY 3, SESSION 2...

Right then, South Africa trail by a hefty 382 runs and are going down the barrel at the moment. They would aim to rebuild from here to at least avoid the follow-on. New Zealand will try to wrap them up as quickly as possible. Stay tuned as we bring you the post-Lunch session which will begin at 6:10 am IST (12:40 am GMT).

Matt Henry is up for a quick chat. He says that the first hour set the tone for them. Adds that they discussed that a few early wickets would help them and they were able to do that which has put them in a good position. Tells that they also talked about improving in some areas. Mentions that there is some seam, but no swing as it is gusty out there. Praise Santner for the way he has bowled, and to see turn and bounce is a good thing for them, and also Ravindra getting in it as well. Ends by saying that he will look how Lunch goes, and then maybe they will think about the follow-on.

Meanwhile, New Zealand's bowlers, led by Matt Henry and Tim Southee, made an impressive start, generating movement with the ball. Henry's strategic setup against Bedingham paid off as he consistently bowled back-of-a-length deliveries, eventually dismissing him and Ruan. Jamieson also posed constant threats with his ability to swing the ball both ways, keeping the batters under pressure throughout the session. Mitchell Santner was surely brilliant and hitting good areas, getting a good purchase off the deck. He got the better of Fortuin. Tim Southee was excellent as a skipper the way he rotated his bowlers and also with the field setup. They do have a huge lead still up their sleeves and would aim to bundle up the Proteas as soon as possible after the Lunch.

LUNCH, DAY 3. SESSION SUMMARY - 28 Overs, 49 Runs, and 3 wickets. Another dominant session for the hosts as the players head to Lunch on Day 3. New Zealand held the advantage and controlled the game's tempo. Bedingham and Petersen resumed the South African innings, but Bedingham's stay at the crease was short-lived as he fell victim to a poor shot early in the day. Ruan de Swardt followed him back to the pavilion in the same over, intensifying the pressure on the visiting team. Keegan Petersen is the only one who resisted pretty well against the Kiwi bowlers and cashed on the chances he got. Clyde Fortuin found himself walking a tightrope. He perished on 9 off a soft dismissal. Keegan Petersen resisted pretty well against the Kiwi bowlers and stands unbeaten on 33. He well cashed on the chances he got. South Africa desperately need a partnership to flourish to at least avoid the follow-on.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start Day 3! The players are already out in the middle. David Bedingham and Keegan Petersen are the overnight batters for South Africa. Tim Southee to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

After toiling for nearly two days against the Kiwi batsmen, the Proteas skipper Neil Brand took a remarkable 6-wicket haul and dismissed the tailenders quickly. Tshepo Moreki and Dane Paterson claimed one wicket each, while Ruan de Swardt snatched a couple. However, the Proteas' batting faltered, with partnerships failing to materialize, leaving them at 80/4 by the end of the second day. Despite decent starts from Zubayr Hamza and Edward Moore, wickets couldn't be preserved. Keegan Petersen will resume batting alongside David Bedingham on the third day and aim to solidify the partnership. Stay tuned as the live-action begins pretty soon.

Welcome to our coverage of Day 3 of the first Test match between New Zealand and South Africa at the picturesque Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui. The hosts have dominated the first two days, posting a commanding total of 511 runs on the back of Rachin Ravindra's superb 240 and Kane Williamson's elegant 118, supported by valuable contributions from the middle order. New Zealand batted for 144 overs until the third session of the second day. The bowlers then maintained the pressure, claiming quick wickets against the new-look Proteas side. Kyle Jamieson took two wickets in a single over, while Matt Henry and Mitchell Santner chipped in with one each.
...DAY 3, SESSION 1...

Right then, we have witnessed two days of solid Test cricketing action but Day 3 is generally known as the moving day and we will surely get a big picture about how this game is going to turn out. South Africa still trail by a massive 431 runs but have a couple of batters with some Test pedigree under their belt. Their main objective will be to try and avoid the follow-on whereas New Zealand will look to make their mark with the ball early on Day 3. Do join us on Tuesday at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT) for the action but you can also catch our build-up which will begin a lot sooner. Cheers!

South Africa were made to toil hard in the field but they did a fine job in the second hour after Lunch as they were able to pick up wickets in a bunch and it was the skipper, Neil Brand who ran through the Kiwi tail and finished with 6 wickets on debut. When they came out to bat though, it was the skipper who was the first to fall and the other debutant Raynard van Tonder got out right after. Edward Moore the third debutant in the top order played well and played his shots but got out in the 20s leaving the visitors reeling at 30/3. The two players who did have Test experience, Zubayr Hamza and David Bedingham countered well and looked all set to see their side through to Day 3 but Hamza got out in an unfortunate way and they had to rebuild again in the last 30 minutes or so. Bedingham along with Keegan Petersen did manage to remain unscathed but they have a big job to do on Day 3.

SESSION SUMMARY - 31 overs, 116 runs and 7 wickets. The game seemed like a slow boiler on Day 1 and for about half of Day 2 as well but after Lunch, gears shifted and we witnessed some excellent action. First, it was the double ton from Rachin Ravindra and then some fireworks from Matt Henry with the bat that took New Zealand past the 500-run mark. With the ball then, Tim Southee and Matt Henry bowled well but it was Kyle Jamieson who came back from injury and bowled a wonderful spell, picking up a couple of wickets that got the Kiwis going. Henry then came back and got one himself after which they faced a bit of resistance. Mitchell Santner bowled tight lines and was rewarded with a lucky breakthrough and the hosts will be quite pleased with how things ended on Day 2.
Turns into the batter on a length, Keegan Petersen goes inside the crease and defends it back to the bowler. And that's a wrap for Day 2.
